text:
**LiFePO4 (LFP) is the better choice for most buyers.** Almost every current power station uses it, and NMC mostly survives in older or very compact models.

**Where LiFePO4 wins**
- **Cycle life:** This is the biggest gap. LFP stations are typically rated for 3,000-6,000 cycles, versus roughly 500-1,000 for NMC in most sources. At one full cycle a day, that is about 8+ years versus under 2 ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/), [OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)). One source claims 1,000-2,000 for NMC ([PowerStationMatch](https://powerstationmatch.com/learn/lifepo4-vs-nmc)), but the spec-based data points lower.
- **Failure behavior:** In lab tests, LFP cells peaked at much lower temperatures when they failed (about 259°C versus 731°C in one study) ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)). It isn't fireproof, though. In one overcharge test the LFP cell reached thermal runaway earlier, but its failure was milder, with smoke and no flames ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/)). That matters for a unit kept indoors or in a vehicle.
- **Price:** The premium is largely gone. One retailer's data shows a median of $0.55/Wh for LFP versus $0.95/Wh for NMC ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)).

**Where NMC wins**
- **Energy density:** NMC cells are denser, but the gap shrinks a lot in finished stations. Across one database, the median NMC unit held only about 10% more Wh per pound ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)). Some sites claim 20-30% lighter, which looks overstated for real products. Compare actual weights rather than assuming.

**Cold weather isn't a differentiator.** Most stations of either chemistry refuse to charge below 32°F, so check the manual for your model ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc), [Enough Watts](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)).

**How to decide**
- **Daily or frequent use (van, off-grid, solar):** LiFePO4.
- **Indoor home backup:** LiFePO4.
- **Rare use where weight matters:** Either one. Compare specific models.
- **Already own a working NMC unit:** Keep using it.
